overview.headline: Balanced and unbalanced forces govern aircraft rise fall and acceleration

keyPoints.point: rules for simplified motion of an aircraft are shown with one force balanced at a time
keyPoints.quote: This page shows some rules for the simplified motion of an aircraft.

keyPoints.point: aircraft will maintain constant cruise velocity when weight balanced by lift and drag balanced by thrust
keyPoints.quote: In this situation, the aircraft will maintain at a constant cruise velocity as described by Newton’s first law of motion.

keyPoints.point: unbalanced forces cause aircraft to move in direction of greater force
keyPoints.quote: If the forces become unbalanced, the aircraft will move in the direction of the greater force.

keyPoints.point: net force is difference between opposing forces lift minus weight or thrust minus drag
keyPoints.quote: The net force is the difference between the opposing forces; lift minus weight, or thrust minus drag.

keyTerms.gloss: rate of change of velocity driven by net force acting on aircraft
keyTerms.quote: Where a is the acceleration, m is the mass of the aircraft, and F is the net force acting on the aircraft.

keyTerms.gloss: quantity of matter in aircraft that determines acceleration from net force
keyTerms.quote: Where a is the acceleration, m is the mass of the aircraft, and F is the net force acting on the aircraft.

keyTerms.gloss: upward force that when greater than weight makes airplane rise
